correctness.rationale: Directly reconstruct E=sum_{k=1}^5|sum_{j=0}^{5-k}exp(i(theta_{j+k}-theta_j))|² and its derivatives. For each lag C, A=sum u_j(e_{j+k}-e_j), B=sum u_j d_j d_j^T, gradient=2Re(i A conjugate C) and Hessian=2Re(-conjugate C B + A conjugate A^T). Independent fresh symbolic computation from ζ=e^{iπ/3} and phase exponents (0,0,1,3,0,4) recovered all five sidelobe unit norms, E=5, exactly zero gradient, the stated 6x6 integer H and exact characteristic polynomial λ²(λ−1)(λ−5)(λ−9)(λ−21). The common-phase and linear-phase zero vectors span the nullspace; positive other four eigenvalues give strict local minimum on the normal slice modulo symmetries. Parseval gives ||P||_4^4=36+2E and doubled Hessian spectrum. This is local; global value 5 is not inferred here.
residual_risks: Exact Hessian eigenvalues depend on Euclidean coordinates on six phases; strict positivity modulo symmetries is intrinsic.

value.rationale: The canonical generalized Barker six-sequence is a natural polyphase design and base-energy benchmark. The exact four positive transverse eigenvalues rigorously measure phase stability and condition number of this known optimum modulo the unavoidable two symmetries; they distinguish a nondegenerate minimum from a merely flat global minimizer. This is a motivated local-stability invariant, not a replacement for or novelty claim about the already-known global energy 5.
residual_risks: Spectrum is local and Euclidean phase-metric dependent; not a bound for arbitrarily large phase changes.

limitations: No proof claimed of global optimum E=5; the global minimum is separately published and its proof not reconstructed in this record.
